reason: The conclusion holds: there is no new mechanism that could be tested honestly and adopted before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC, and the expected gain is about 0. Three of the stated reasons need correcting. (a) Cost is right: exp60 took shard A 6,959 s + shard B 5,599 s = 3.49 GPU-h (CONTEXT 20:05Z). But lowrefine is not a node-adding arm: raw nodes stay at 121,777, and final nodes vs K1 change by +0.004 / +0.118 / 0 / +0.013% (dummy gates, 17:20Z). So the node-count lab bias (round 3, fact 16) is the wrong reason. The real reasons: (1) lowrefine needs GPU head features, so no CPU replay is possible; (2) coordinate gains in the lab do not transfer: floatout scored +0.0023 on the x138 lab but tied twice on the LB (P32, P33); (3) any read would be post hoc against the READ TABLE committed in 1017c41. Lowrefine is the one component shared by F1 and F2 and not hedged (lens_private-finals: size ~0.0002, P(>=0) 0.6-0.8). Still, the only scored alternative without it is exp52 (0.950), so the value of the information is about 0. (b) Right: v_divisions-x138_d1 (value) is refuted with 'moves no decision'; R2 was decided on the LB, and finals = max(K2, twin) already hedge the insertion. (c) Right: R3S-2 is in round3 'rejected'. R4H-6's Q0 concentration is in-sample, and dense-half precision 2/6 is not a margin that is safe out of fold. (d) Mislabelled: fork-only removal riders (the C04/forkmid class) fall under R3, not R4. Both classes need a public read plus a lab gate, and every gate on this 56-clip bed has failed (forkmid, forkblob, ANTIPAR, DNVETO, K3b). The bed is also worn out by repeated mining, so the conclusion stands. One omission: floatout on x138 (I-215) is still listed as 'optional, needs OK' in KNOWLEDGE/DECISIONS.md l.96-98, while the CONTEXT RESUME POINT (l.2022) lists 'float output' as CLOSED. Its E(private) is ~+0.0001, and exactly 0 if the server rounds or casts (P ~0.8-0.9). FLOATOUT_CHECK is a bare assert, so it is not fail-soft. Using it would also mean an S12 file replacing the already-scored K2. Net value is about 0 with nonzero risk. So it does not refute R4H-7, but the conflicting status should be settled. Feasibility: the action is 'do nothing', which is trivially byte-identical and consistent with R8/R9, with no runtime cost.

Lowrefine is the only unhedged component common to both finals (~0.0002), and the only scored alternative without it is exp52.' (3) In (d), write 'R3/R4 riders both need a public read'. (4) Settle floatout: add a dated CONTEXT line closing floatout on x138 for the finals (E ~+0.0001; the check is not fail-soft; it would displace the scored K2 through an S12 build), and update KNOWLEDGE I-215 to match. If the user wants it anyway, it goes on the morning OK list, with the fail-soft port finished before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC (R8).
realistic_gain: 0 on public and private. The finding is correct that nothing should be built; the wording fixes only prevent misreadings (slot carve-outs, and the floatout status conflict between CONTEXT and KNOWLEDGE).
